researched.name: Modison Ltd
researched.trigger: price: Silver — WPI Silver Apr-2026 index 440.5, +152.4% y/y; silver import unit price (HS 710691) US$1,903.8/kg in Jul-2026, +85.1% on last-3m vs year-ago-3m
researched.reason: Exposure verified in the company's own documents: the FY26 annual report names the raw material ('Basic ingredients of company raw material is Silver and Tungsten Powder'), states 'The company is able to pass on price hike to the customer' via long-term supply contracts and price-sharing arrangements, and reports a single segment, 'Manufacturing of Electrical Contacts'. Materials are 87.1% of FY26 revenue and 91.1% of Q1 FY27 revenue, so revenue is largely pass-through metal value. Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 270.47 cr (+102% YoY) with PAT Rs 33.84 cr vs Rs 4.80 cr, and gross margin up from 17.6% to 39.1%. Silver hedging is disclosed separately as an exceptional item (+Rs 2.61 cr FY26, -Rs 0.39 cr Q1 FY27), so the gain is conversion margin on a higher metal base rather than an unhedged inventory revaluation — a documented correction to the map's 'inventory revalues' wording. Published with the caveat, measured this run, that silver is -3.0% over 1 month and -11.0% over 3 months on WPI and -3.5%/-1.1% on spot: the uplift is a year-on-year level effect already in the numbers, not a live move.

researched.name: Sugs Lloyd Ltd
researched.trigger: filing: ORDER — Letter of Award 22-Sep-2026 from M/s Marshal Enterprises, Rs 213.48 cr incl GST, LT/HT loss-reduction works under RDSS in Punjab (originally awarded by PSPCL), back-to-back, 15 months
researched.reason: Hard trigger with a number, read in the filing itself. Ex-GST about Rs 180.9 cr over 15 months against FY26 revenue of Rs 300.73 cr. It is the third large award in three weeks: Rs 214.27 cr (TPSODL/TPWODL, 1-Sep), Rs 24.63 cr (TPCODL, 3-Sep) and today's Rs 213.48 cr — roughly Rs 452 cr of fresh awards against Rs 58.37 cr in all of Q1 FY27 and an order book of Rs 807 cr at 30-Jun-2026. Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 78.40 cr (+32%), EBITDA margin 15.3%, PAT Rs 7.50 cr. Management guides to Rs 600 cr FY27 and Rs 1,000 cr FY28 at an unchanged margin, which puts the stock at 10.5x and 6.3x the 22-Sep close — but Q1 was only 13% of the FY27 target, so the guidance needs 2.2x the Q1 run-rate for three quarters. CRISIL assigned BBB/Stable and A3+ on Rs 225 cr of facilities on 26-Aug-2026 and flags 245-day receivables and 265-day gross current assets. Published with those two risks stated.

researched.name: Parmeshwar Metal Ltd
researched.trigger: price: Copper — LME copper US$14,788/t on 21-Sep-2026, +24.4% over 6 months and at 98% of its 52-week range; copper scrap import unit price (HS 7404) US$9.54/kg in Jul-2026, +36.6% y/y
researched.reason: The copper exposure is documented — the FY26 annual report states the company 'is engaged in the business of manufacturing and trading of copper wire and copper wire rods by recycling of copper scrap', so effectively 100% of revenue is copper, and FY26 revenue rose 42.7% to Rs 1,972.94 cr with PAT up 196% to Rs 32.49 cr. Three things stopped it at the bar. First, three separate GST enforcement orders, all alleging inadmissible input tax credit: DRC-07 received 26-Mar-2026 (tax Rs 3.43 cr plus interest and penalties Rs 7.44 cr) and 15-Apr-2026 (tax Rs 1.59 cr plus penalties Rs 6.07 cr), both from the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (Enforcement), Gandhinagar, for 'alleged inadmissible ITC received from non-existent suppliers / tax defaulters', and an Order in Appeal received 15-Jun-2026 confirming tax of Rs 1,34,92,864 plus interest and an equal penalty for 'alleged inadmissible / fraudulent ITC received'. Tax plus stated penalties total roughly Rs 21 cr against FY26 PAT of Rs 32.49 cr; the company is appealing and says it foresees no material impact. For a scrap-sourcing recycler this goes to the quality of revenue, not just to a tax number. Second, the annual report discloses no installed capacity, tonnage or utilisation anywhere, so the physical revenue model the method requires cannot be built. Third, the map's 'inventory gains' mechanic is weak here as a matter of record: total inventory at 31-Mar-2026 was about Rs 37.8 cr on Rs 1,972.94 cr of revenue (roughly 7 days), and cost of material consumed was 97.2% of revenue, so the earnings driver is the scrap-to-rod conversion spread and volume, not metal held on the balance sheet. Revisit if the appeals resolve and the company discloses capacity.

researched.name: Diffusion Engineers Ltd
researched.trigger: price: Tungsten — export unit price for HS 284180 (sodium tungstate) +606.5% on a last-3m vs year-ago-3m basis; tungsten waste and scrap (HS 8101) import unit price +280.4% on the same basis
researched.verdict: mapped as beneficiary, measured as sufferer — map corrected, not published
researched.reason: The company's own Q1 FY27 earnings call (13-Aug-2026) contradicts the map entry. Asked about tungsten and rare-earth prices, management said the increase 'was transferred to us and typically it takes some time for us to absorb it and then transfer it to our customers, especially for orders which we have already clocked in… we can't go back to the customer and ask midway for price hikes', that 'some of the ferro-alloys like Tungsten and all have gone up by few hundred percent', and that 'that is basically reflected in our gross margin contraction' — quantified on the call as roughly 1% to 1.5% of gross margin in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27. Tungsten is an input here, not a product, and pass-through is lagged. Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 95.91 cr (+30.7% YoY) but PAT fell to Rs 9.98 cr from Rs 14.20 cr, and the stock trades at a BSE-header PE of 40.92. Per the playbook this is a watch-and-red-flag line, not a short idea, and DIFFNKG has been moved from 'benefit' to 'suffer' in the tungsten group of docs/ideas/commodity_map.json with the transcript cited as the reason. The tungsten group now lists no small-cap beneficiary.

map_changes: tungsten: DIFFNKG moved from benefit to suffer, citing the 13-Aug-2026 Q1 FY27 earnings call where management attributes gross-margin contraction of about 1-1.5 percentage points to tungsten and ferro-alloy prices that could not be passed through on booked orders
watch: Paper (strength 4.31, up): the group's evidence is the import unit price of HS 4707 waste paper, +43.1% in one month and +9.3% over three. Rising waste-paper prices are an INPUT cost for recycled-paper mills, while WPI Paper for printing & writing is only +2.0% over one month — so the mapped producers (JKPAPER, WSTCSTPAPR, ANDHRAPAP, SESHAPAPER) are margin sufferers on this evidence, not beneficiaries, unless finished-paper prices follow. Tamil Nadu Newsprint & Papers (TNPL, in the universe at Rs 986 cr) filed a CareEdge credit-rating report on 21-Sep-2026 and was not researched this run. The paper group's benefit/suffer mapping needs the same document check that corrected tungsten.

Silver (strength 10.16, up): the score is driven by a 12-month comparison. On 1-month and 3-month windows silver is negative on both WPI (-3.0%, -11.0%) and spot (-3.5%, -1.1%). Any silver-linked idea should be framed as a level effect, not momentum.

Copper (strength 5.25, up) is the opposite: LME copper is at 98% of its 52-week range, +5.3% in a week and +24.4% over six months. This is the live move in the panel and the one to keep researching as small-cap names are verified.

Tungsten (strength 10.0, up): the export unit price for HS 284180 is +606.5% on the smoothed year-on-year measure but -43.4% over one month and -36.8% over three on HS 8101, on a small base of US$8.6 mn per month of exports — the recent direction is down and the codes are thin.
data_problems: Sandbox egress blocked three of the four commodity builders. spot.py (Westmetall + Markets Insider), wpi.py (eaindustry.nic.in) and trade.py --latest (tradestat.commerce.gov.in) all failed with 'Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden' at the proxy; a direct curl to each host returns 000 while www.bseindia.com returns 200. The committed panels were left exactly as they were: spot.json still carries its 2026-09-22 17:20 IST build, wpi.json.gz its Apr-2026 index and trade/ its 2026-07 month built at 2026-09-22 18:36 IST, so signals.py ran on current data. spot.py had overwritten spot.json and spot_series.json with an empty 0-row build before the failure was caught; both files were restored to their committed content with a file-scoped git checkout and are unchanged in this commit.

signals.py stamps signals.json's 'built' field with the container clock labelled IST (it wrote '2026-09-22 14:06 IST' for a run at 19:36 IST). The cloud VM runs UTC. The field is off by 5h30m on cloud runs; the builder needs a TZ fix, which is outside this run's permitted paths (scripts/ideas/).

Modison's Q1 FY27 result PDF and annual report are not extracted by dossier.py (it reported 'docs 0'); both were downloaded and read directly from BSE with PyMuPDF for this run. The related-party transaction table in the Modison annual report extracts with its columns misaligned, so the actual FY26 value transacted with Modison Copper Private Limited is recorded as unknown; only the approved omnibus limit of Rs 80 cr a year is cited.
note: Two ideas published. The price-driven half ran first, as the playbook requires: of the 32 groups at or above the strength threshold, only four mapped to a beneficiary inside the Rs 200-2,000 cr universe that was worth the deep work, and two of those four were researched to a negative verdict from the companies' own documents — Parmeshwar Metal on unresolved GST enforcement orders alleging input tax credit from non-existent suppliers, and Diffusion Engineers where the earnings call shows tungsten is an input that compressed gross margin rather than a pass-through benefit. The tungsten map entry was corrected accordingly.
